media: Below is a video of someone playing it: the first evening of the season in full (at one point the player zooms all the way in for a low view), then a montage of later evenings (each one shown from its opening and then from just before the sun sets), ending with the last minute of a night watch.
first_impression: This is Untitled Goose Game meets classic sheepdog trials, and it actually understands how sheep herding works. The soft pastoral aesthetic caught my eye immediately, but seeing mechanics like eye-stalking, creeping, and genuine wolf-defense tension sold me that it's an actual game and not just cozy fluff.
best_things: The influence radius and posture mechanics (creeping, lying down, flanking) capture genuine border collie instincts instead of feeling like generic push-physics.
Every evening introduces a distinct mechanical hook, from sheep trials and lost lambs to flooding rivers, stubborn rams, and snowstorms.
The transition into dusk when the wolves emerge turns a relaxing pastoral simulator into genuine, high-stakes tactical triage.

worst_problems.problem: The low third-person camera angle completely ruins navigation and sightlines compared to the clean top-down view.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the camera in an isometric or top-down perspective permanently, or add an explicit toggle so players don't get stuck behind trees and walls when precision matters.

worst_problems.problem: The red wolf attack banner and picture-in-picture snatch cam look clunky and shatter the clean, organic presentation.
worst_problems.suggestion: Replace the giant emergency banner and pop-up video with audio distress bleats and a clean directional threat indicator on the field.

worst_problems.problem: Sheep bottlenecking and getting stuck around pen gates turns an otherwise fluid drive into tedious micro-nudging.
worst_problems.suggestion: Tweak sheep boids attraction near the open pen entrance so they draw each other in once the first couple cross the threshold.

worst_problems.problem: The minimap in the top right looks like a flat programmer placeholder that clashes with the painterly 3D environment.
worst_problems.suggestion: Redraw the minimap in the style of an inked vintage Ordnance Survey or shepherd's hand-drawn field map.

worst_problems.problem: The stamina bar and key prompt HUD at the bottom left and center feel crowded and constantly draw the eye away from the field.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fade the control prompts once the player demonstrates the input, and integrate the stamina gauge subtly into Pip's influence ring.

boredom_points: 02:30 - 02:50 when four ewes stall right outside the gate during the trial and require tiny micro-adjustments back and forth.
08:00 - 08:20 during the mist level when you spend long stretches just walking down an empty dirt track searching for bleat pings.
confusions: How close Pip can get to a wolf before taking damage or getting attacked directly.
Whether barking has a cooldown penalty or if it permanently spooks the sheep into a disorganized panic.
wish_list: Whistle commands and traditional shepherd whistle audio cues mapped to hotkeys.
A free-play sandbox mode where you can customize field layouts, flock sizes, and predator spawn rates.
Different dog breeds or cosmetic coats (like a red border collie or rough collie).
one_line_review: A gorgeous, surprisingly tense border collie simulator that trades cozy gimmickry for authentic herding mechanics.
